thread:
maya: Quick ping — just ran the first onboard pass for lichen-v1 (fp16 vs int8 per-channel) on short-query holdout. Seeing recall@10 drop from 0.84 -> 0.71 for int8, silhouette score also dropped ~0.06. Not massive but suspicious. Anyone else seeing this pattern?

ravi: ack. can you paste the eval command and sample config?

maya: sure — run was:```bash
python eval/recall.py --model lichen-v1 --quant int8_ppq --holdout shorttail.csv --k 10 --batch 512
```

eli: hmm batch 512 is big for short queries, but that shouldn't change embedding values. did you apply the same whitening/normalization steps?

maya: yes, we run mean-centering + l2 norm in postproc. config snippet:```json
{"whiten": true, "norm": "l2", "use_kvcache": false}
```

ravi: any hints in the per-cohort breakdown? maybe long-tail vs canonical queries diverge.

maya: breakdown attached in the run summary (pasted below). shorttail recall@10: fp16 0.84, int8 0.71. medium queries: fp16 0.88, int8 0.86. long queries: fp16 0.81, int8 0.79. so most degradation on short queries. silhouette: fp16 0.42 -> int8 0.36. cluster sizes look similar but centroids shift for high-frequency anchors.

eli: that suggests quantization noise on high-similarity small-context vectors. did you try per-channel vs per-tensor quant?

maya: per-channel used (ppq per-channel symmetric). per-tensor looked worse. we also tried clamp to 6 bits earlier and saw catastrophic collapse.

ravi: could be dynamic range mismatch for embeddings dominated by few dims. try per-channel percentile clipping (99.9) before quant and re-eval. also run a tiny-batch job with batch=32 to rule out microbatching K/V cache interaction.

maya: running now:```bash
python eval/recall.py --model lichen-v1 --quant int8_ppq --clip 99.9 --holdout shorttail.csv --k 10 --batch 32 --save-run tmp/lichen_clip99p.json
```

ops-bot: job queued on eval-workers-7. estimated finish ~2m.

(test-bot): automated check summary for run 1744209876-1: metrics: recall@10 0.78, silhouette 0.39, centroid-shift-mean 0.042. (compared to baseline fp16 recall@10 0.84). flagged: short-query drift, anchor-centroid-shift > 0.03 :warning:

eli: okay clip helped but not restored. can we try reconstruction error per-dim and rank the dims by sensitivity? i suspect top-5 dims encode stopword-ish signal that get flattened by quantization.

maya: I ran quick PCA residuals on the shorttail set: top 3 dims explain 28% variance; quant L2 error concentrated in dims [1,3,7]. attaching tiny table: fp16->int8 mse per-dim: [0.002, 0.018, 0.001, 0.022, 0.0009, ...]

ravi: interesting. propose two follow-ups: 1) bias-correct those sensitive channels (store small float offset post-quant), 2) try asymmetric per-channel quant (scale + zero-point) to reduce error on those dims and re-run cluster sanity.

maya: will try both. starting with asymmetric per-channel:```bash
python quantize/convert.py --model lichen-v1 --mode asymmetric_perchannel --clip 99.9 --out lichen-int8-asym.pt
python eval/recall.py --model lichen-int8-asym --holdout shorttail.csv --k 10 --batch 64
```

(test-bot): run 1744209876-2 completed. recall@10 0.82, silhouette 0.41, centroid-shift-mean 0.018. regression delta vs fp16 now within noise for shorttail.

ravi: great! can you push the asymmetric recipe into the quant recommendations for lichen-v1? also add an automated check that flags centroid-shift > 0.03 for short-query cohorts during onboarding.

maya: will update the onboarding doc and the Optimize suggestions. quick note: asymmetric increased model size slightly and add a bit of decode CPU cost, but unit token cost change negligible.

eli: thanks — let's mark as resolved for now but add a follow-up ticket to test on multilingual holdouts (might behave differently).

maya: created ticket INF-7291 and linked the runs in the onboarding page. closing thread. :white_check_mark:
